description: Control real web browsers using Python to scrape dynamic sites and automate workflows.

slides.title: Why Browser Automation?
slides.content:
# The Limits of Requests 🚧

`requests` and `Scrapy` download raw HTML. But modern websites are heavily reliant on JavaScript (React, Vue, Angular).

If the data you want to scrape is injected into the page by JavaScript *after* the initial HTML loads, `requests` will just see an empty `<div>`!

To scrape these sites, you must run a real web browser that executes the JavaScript. Enter **Browser Automation**.

slides.title: What is Selenium?
slides.content:
# Selenium WebDriver 🚗

Selenium is a widely used tool for automating web browsers. It requires a "Driver" (like ChromeDriver or GeckoDriver) to talk to the specific browser installed on your computer.

## Installation
```bash
pip install selenium
```

## Basic Setup
```python_not
from selenium import webdriver

# Open a Chrome window
driver = webdriver.Chrome()

# Navigate to a URL
driver.get("https://google.com")

# Get the page title
print(driver.title)

# Close the browser
driver.quit()
```

slides.title: Finding Elements
slides.content:
# Locating Elements 🔍

Once the browser loads the page, you can find elements to interact with using the `By` class.

```python_not
from selenium.webdriver.common.by import By

# Find by ID
element = driver.find_element(By.ID, "submit-button")

# Find by CSS Selector
element = driver.find_element(By.CSS_SELECTOR, ".product-title")

# Find by XPath
element = driver.find_element(By.XPATH, "//div[@class='nav']/a[1]")

# Find MULTIPLE elements
elements = driver.find_elements(By.CLASS_NAME, "item")
```

slides.title: Interacting with Elements
slides.content:
# Clicking and Typing ⌨️

Unlike BeautifulSoup which only reads data, Selenium can *interact* with the webpage!

```python_not
from selenium.webdriver.common.keys import Keys

search_box = driver.find_element(By.NAME, "q")

# Type text into the input field
search_box.send_keys("Python Web Scraping")

# Press the ENTER key
search_box.send_keys(Keys.RETURN)

# Click a button
login_btn = driver.find_element(By.ID, "login")
login_btn.click()
```

slides.title: Explicit and Implicit Waits
slides.content:
# Waiting for Elements ⏳

Because JavaScript loads elements asynchronously, an element might not exist the millisecond the `driver.get()` finishes.
If you try to click it immediately, your script crashes!

## Implicit Wait (Global)
Tells WebDriver to poll the DOM for a certain amount of time when trying to find *any* element.
```python_not
driver.implicitly_wait(10) # wait up to 10 seconds
```

## Explicit Wait (Specific)
Wait for a specific condition on a specific element.
```python_not
from selenium.webdriver.support.ui import WebDriverWait
from selenium.webdriver.support import expected_conditions as EC

# Wait up to 10 seconds until the element is clickable
element = WebDriverWait(driver, 10).until(
    EC.element_to_be_clickable((By.ID, 'myDynamicElement'))
)
```

slides.title: Knowledge Check: Selenium
slides.quizQuestion: Why is it important to use 'Waits' when automating a browser?
quizOptions: To prevent the browser from using too much RAM.
Because elements loaded via JavaScript might not exist immediately after the HTML finishes loading.
To slow down the script so the user can watch what is happening.

slides.title: ActionChains
slides.content:
# Complex Interactions 🖱️

Sometimes you need to do more than just click. You need to hover, drag-and-drop, or perform complex key combinations.

Use `ActionChains`!

```python_not
from selenium.webdriver import ActionChains

menu = driver.find_element(By.ID, "dropdown-menu")
submenu = driver.find_element(By.ID, "submenu-item")

# Hover over the menu, wait for submenu, then click it
actions = ActionChains(driver)
actions.move_to_element(menu)
actions.click(submenu)
actions.perform()  # Don't forget to call perform()!
```

slides.title: Headless Mode
slides.content:
# Invisible Browsers 👻

Running automated tests or scraping scripts with a visible browser window popping up is annoying, especially on a server (which doesn't have a screen!).

You can run browsers in **Headless Mode**.

```python_not
from selenium.webdriver.chrome.options import Options

chrome_options = Options()
chrome_options.add_argument("--headless")
# Often required on Linux servers
chrome_options.add_argument("--no-sandbox") 

driver = webdriver.Chrome(options=chrome_options)
```

slides.title: What is Playwright?
slides.content:
# The New Challenger 🎭

While Selenium is the industry standard, **Playwright** (built by Microsoft) is rapidly gaining popularity.

Why Playwright?
- It doesn't require downloading separate WebDrivers.
- It has built-in auto-waiting (no more `WebDriverWait`!).
- It supports extremely fast asynchronous execution.
- It has powerful network interception tools.

## Installation
```bash
pip install playwright
playwright install  # Downloads Chromium, Firefox, and WebKit
```

slides.title: Async Playwright
slides.content:
# Async Execution ⚡

Playwright has a synchronous API, but its true power lies in its `async` API, allowing you to run multiple browser contexts concurrently.

```python_not
import asyncio
from playwright.async_api import async_playwright

async def main():
    async with async_playwright() as p:
        # Launch Chromium
        browser = await p.chromium.launch(headless=False)
        page = await browser.new_page()
        
        await page.goto('http://whatsmyuseragent.org/')
        
        # Take a screenshot
        await page.screenshot(path='example.png')
        await browser.close()

asyncio.run(main())
```

slides.title: Auto-waiting in Playwright
slides.content:
# Smart Waiting 🧠

Unlike Selenium where you must manually wait for elements, Playwright auto-waits for elements to be actionable (visible, stable, enabled) before performing actions!

```python_not
# This will automatically wait until the #submit button 
# exists, is visible, and is no longer moving or disabled.
await page.click('#submit')

# Fill out a form (auto-waits for the input field)
await page.fill('#email', 'user@example.com')
```

slides.title: Knowledge Check: Playwright
slides.quizQuestion: Which of the following is a major advantage of Playwright over Selenium?
quizOptions: It automatically waits for elements to be actionable before interacting with them.
It cannot run in headless mode.
It requires downloading third-party WebDrivers manually.

slides.title: Network Interception
slides.content:
# Modifying Network Traffic 🕸️

Playwright allows you to intercept and modify HTTP traffic! You can block images to save bandwidth or mock API responses.

```python_not
# Block all images from loading to speed up scraping
async def intercept_route(route):
    if route.request.resource_type == "image":
        await route.abort()
    else:
        await route.continue_()

await page.route("**/*", intercept_route)
await page.goto("https://amazon.com")
```

slides.title: Device Emulation
slides.content:
# Emulating Mobile Devices 📱

Many websites serve different HTML to mobile devices. Playwright makes it trivially easy to emulate an iPhone or Android.

```python_not
async with async_playwright() as p:
    iphone_12 = p.devices['iPhone 12']
    browser = await p.webkit.launch()
    
    # Create a new context simulating an iPhone 12
    context = await browser.new_context(
        **iphone_12,
        locale='de-DE',        # Fake the location to Germany
        color_scheme='dark'    # Force dark mode
    )
    
    page = await context.new_page()
    await page.goto('https://maps.google.com')
```

slides.title: Evaluating JavaScript
slides.content:
# Injecting JavaScript 💉

Both Selenium and Playwright allow you to execute arbitrary JavaScript inside the browser context.

## Playwright Example
```python_not
# Get the window's scroll height
height = await page.evaluate("document.body.scrollHeight")

# Modify the DOM directly
await page.evaluate("document.body.style.backgroundColor = 'red'")

# Pass variables from Python to JS
result = await page.evaluate("x => x * 2", 5)
```

slides.title: Extracting Data
slides.content:
# Getting the Scraped Data 📦

While you can use `page.evaluate()` to extract text, Playwright provides helper methods.

```python_not
# Get text content of a single element
title = await page.text_content('h1.title')

# Get an attribute
href = await page.get_attribute('a.login', 'href')

# Better yet: Get the full HTML and pass it to BeautifulSoup!
html_content = await page.content()
soup = BeautifulSoup(html_content, 'lxml')
```
Passing the fully rendered HTML to BeautifulSoup is often the fastest way to extract complex data!

slides.title: Summary
slides.content:
# Summary 🎉

You are now a master of browser automation!

## Key Takeaways
- ✅ **Browser Automation:** Necessary for scraping Javascript-rendered applications.
- ✅ **Selenium:** The industry standard. Uses `WebDriverWait` and `ActionChains` for complex interactions.
- ✅ **Playwright:** The modern alternative. Supports `async`, auto-waiting, and requires no external driver downloads.
- ✅ **Headless Mode:** Run browsers invisibly for server deployment.
- ✅ **Network Interception:** Block images/ads or mock API responses using Playwright's `route()` method.
- ✅ **Device Emulation:** Spoof user agents, screen sizes, and geolocation to view mobile versions of websites.
